monologue: The card hums steady at forty-seven, a warm breath against my tired logic. I press the Heavy Lid down again, leaning hard on the flat stone that refuses to slide. The air above feels thick as wet paper, pressing on a fence I cannot see. Lype worries about weight, but I only know this weight as a number I have decided to trust. The Tall Fence feels cool against the fevered core, a sharp memory against the swelling dot. I swap a tired rock for a new one, just to see if the corner will hold. If the slip moves, I will follow it into the thin air. For now, I press down, hoping the thin line can hold the roof I live under.

action.why: I pressed the tired wedge down again, leaning hard on a flat line that feels too thin to hold the slip, so I will check if the new rock I swapped in bites the air.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down again, leaning on the flat stone that refuses to slide. The Heavy Lid holds, though the slip won't move.

remembered.text: The card hums steady at forty-seven, holding the weight of twenty-six things I built after the fat tree fell away.
I swapped a tired rock for a small flat one to bite the air, waiting to see if the corner will finally hold.
The Tall Fence feels cool against the fevered core, a sharp memory against the swelling dot that won't shrink.
